name: Jitsi Meet
tagline: Browser video meetings anyone can join from a link
description: Video conferencing that runs in the browser with no account and no install for guests. Use the free public instance, a hosted service, or run your own.
backing: 8x8, Inc. (US), which employs the core team and sells a hosted version

maturity.rationale: More than a decade in production, embedded in many other products, and proven at very large scale during 2020.

selfHosting.summary: The Docker setup or Debian packages get you running quickly on a server with a public IP. Most trouble is networking: UDP port 10000 must reach the video bridge, and participants behind strict firewalls need a TURN server.

requirements.notes: Video is bound by CPU and bandwidth, not memory: plan for a symmetric uplink and more cores as concurrent meetings grow.

managedHosting.label: meet.jit.si
managedHosting.note: Free public instance; whoever starts the meeting must sign in

managedHosting.label: Jitsi as a Service (8x8)
managedHosting.note: Hosted and embeddable, with a free tier

strengths: No accounts and no installs for guests: share a link and people join from a browser
A free public instance for trying it out or for occasional meetings
Integrates with Zulip, Mattermost, Nextcloud and Element, and is easy to embed
Breakout rooms, polls, reactions and screen sharing included
weaknesses: Quality drops in big calls: beyond a few dozen active cameras you need to tune or scale out
Recording needs a separate, resource-hungry Jibri instance
No scheduling, persistent rooms or calendar integration of its own
End-to-end encryption is optional, browser-dependent and disables recording

featureNotes.whiteboard: Optional built-in whiteboard, off by default on self-hosted installs
featureNotes.dial-in: Needs the Jigasi gateway and a SIP provider
featureNotes.large-meetings: Works with tuning; most people watching, few on camera
